overview: Valdemar IV Atterdag was Danish king who rebuilt royal power after the near-collapse of the kingdom. The profile is anchored by concrete turning points: 1340 — Becomes king; 1361 — Captures Visby.
He died in 1375, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Valdemar IV Atterdag was Danish king who rebuilt royal power after the near-collapse of the kingdom. The profile is anchored by concrete turning points: 1340 — Becomes king; 1361 — Captures Visby.
He died in 1375, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Valdemar IV Atterdag was born c. 1320. His family background is usually placed in House of Estridsen, though early Scandinavian genealogy can be uncertain and politically shaped.

Valdemar IV Atterdag's early life belonged to the medieval Scandinavian world, where kinship, sea routes, church contacts, assemblies, and armed followings shaped the opportunities available to a ruler.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Valdemar IV of Denmark, called Atterdag, is remembered as the cunning restorer of a kingdom that had nearly ceased to exist, and the tradition credits him with exceptional political guile. Inheriting a realm mortgaged to foreign creditors, he reassembled it piece by piece through purchase, marriage, war, and ruthless opportunism, earning a reputation as a wily and relentless operator who recovered Danish royal power almost from nothing.

His methods could be hard and provocative: his sack of Visby on Gotland in 1361 was long remembered for its severity, and his aggressive policies drew the Hanseatic League and Scandinavian rivals into war against him. The byname Atterdag — variously explained as "new day" or "again day" — came to symbolise the dawn he was felt to have brought to Danish fortunes.

The consistent portrait is of a shrewd, determined, and sometimes unscrupulous ruler whose intelligence and persistence rebuilt the monarchy. He is remembered for statecraft rather than warmth — a calculating king who out-thought his enemies and laid the groundwork that his daughter Margaret I would extend into the Kalmar Union.

contentSections.title: As king of Denmark
paragraphs: Valdemar IV recovered territories, strengthened royal authority, and restored Denmark after years of fragmentation. His capture of Visby in 1361 made him powerful but provoked Hanseatic and Scandinavian opposition.
As King of Denmark, Valdemar IV Atterdag had to turn dynastic claim into workable authority through alliances, military pressure, church support, and acceptance by regional elites.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Died at Gurre Castle in 1375; the succession opened the way for Margaret I’s political rise.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: He is remembered as the restorer of medieval Denmark and father of Margaret I.
Later saga, saintly, or national traditions often amplified Valdemar IV Atterdag's reputation, so the article separates near-contemporary evidence from later memory where possible.

timeline.title: Born
timeline.description: Valdemar IV Atterdag was born around c. 1320, but the birthplace is not securely recorded. The date is approximate, but it places the early life in the setting of Kingdom of Denmark.

timeline.title: Becomes king
timeline.description: Valdemar IV took the throne in a fractured Denmark and began rebuilding royal authority after years of pledged lands and weak kingship.

timeline.title: Captures Visby
timeline.description: Valdemar’s conquest of Visby in 1361 showed revived Danish military power but provoked wider Baltic and Hanseatic resistance.

timeline.title: Death
timeline.description: Died at Gurre Castle in 1375; the succession opened the way for Margaret I’s political rise.

timeline.title: Aftermath and memory
timeline.description: Valdemar’s recovery of Danish royal power made possible Margaret I’s later union politics, even though his own male line failed.
